q: A work order issued under a zonal contract for a petty work:

options.A: Creates an altogether new and independent contract for that petty work
options.B: Authorises the execution of that specific petty work under, and on the rates and conditions of, the zonal contract already in force
options.C: Dispenses with the need for recording measurements of the petty work
options.D: Is issued by the contractor to the Engineer for starting the work

e: A work order under a zonal contract only authorises a specific petty work on the rates and conditions of the zonal contract already in force; it is not a new independent contract.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A work order under a zonal contract authorises the contractor to execute a specified petty work covered by that contract.
2. A running account bill is a bill for payment of the value of work actually measured and executed by a contractor during the progress of a work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a zonal work order authorises a specified petty work under that contract, and a running account bill is for payment of work actually measured and executed during progress of the work.

q: Payment made to a contractor against a running account (on-account) bill is in the nature of:

options.A: An interim payment for the work measured so far, adjustable at the final settlement of the contract
options.B: Final settlement of all his claims under the contract
options.C: An advance given before any work has been executed by him
options.D: Payment of compensation for delay in completion of the work

e: Payment on a running account or on-account bill is an interim payment for work measured so far, adjustable at final settlement; it is neither final settlement nor an advance before execution.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The internal check of a contractor's bill by the Accounts office covers the sanction for the work, the agreement and rates, the measurements recorded and the recoveries due.
2. Before passing a bill, the Accounts office itself re-measures the work at the site in place of the executive officers.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Accounts internal check covers sanction, agreement and rates, measurements and recoveries due; Accounts does not itself re-measure work at site in place of the executive.

q: A successful tenderer is issued the Letter of Acceptance for a work but thereafter fails to execute the formal agreement and does not commence the work. In such a case, the Railways may:

options.A: Award the work to him again at enhanced rates
options.B: Recover the loss only from the earnest money of the other tenderers
options.C: Wait indefinitely until the tenderer chooses to start the work
options.D: Cancel the acceptance and forfeit his Earnest Money Deposit, in accordance with the tender conditions

e: If the successful tenderer fails to execute the agreement and commence work after Letter of Acceptance, Railways may cancel the acceptance and forfeit his Earnest Money Deposit per the tender conditions.

q: Where the authority competent to accept a tender does not agree with the recommendation of the Tender Committee, the accepting authority should:

options.A: Accept the recommendation in every case, as it has no power to differ from it
options.B: Record its reasons in writing for differing from the recommendation of the Tender Committee
options.C: Return the case to the contractor for his remarks
options.D: Refer the tender to another Tender Committee for a fresh recommendation in all cases

e: An accepting authority differing from the Tender Committee recommendation must record its reasons in writing for differing; it cannot silently override or accept in every case.

q: The member of a Tender Committee drawn from a department other than the executive department dealing with the work primarily serves to:

options.A: Prepare the detailed estimate of the work
options.B: Bring an independent viewpoint, unconnected with the sponsoring executive department, to the examination of the tenders
options.C: Record the measurements of the work after it is awarded
options.D: Fix the rates to be quoted by the tenderers

e: The member from a department other than the executive department brings an independent viewpoint, unconnected with the sponsoring department, to examination of tenders in the Tender Committee.

q: A work requires a specialised item of equipment-cum-execution obtainable only from the original manufacturer, who alone can execute it to the required specification. Inviting a single tender from that firm in such a case is in order when:

options.A: The division finds open tendering time-consuming as a matter of routine
options.B: Only one contractor is enlisted in the division for works in general
options.C: The proprietary or special nature of the requirement is recorded, Finance concurs and the competent authority approves the single tender
options.D: The work is of high value and is to be completed quickly

e: Single tender from the original manufacturer is in order only when the proprietary or special nature is recorded, Finance concurs and the competent authority approves; routine time-saving is not a ground.

q: In a works tender, the lowest offer received is somewhat higher than the sanctioned estimate, but the Tender Committee finds the rates reasonable with reference to the last accepted rates and the prevailing market rates. The Committee may:

options.A: Reject the tender invariably, since any rate above the estimate is unreasonable
options.B: Direct the tenderer to reduce his rates to the estimate rates as a condition of award
options.C: Award the work at the estimate rates without the tenderer's consent
options.D: Recommend acceptance of the offer, recording the justification for the reasonableness of the rates, with the concurrence of Finance

e: The Tender Committee may recommend acceptance of the lowest offer even above the estimate if rates are justified as reasonable with reference to last accepted rates and market rates, with Finance concurrence.

q: The completion of a work is delayed solely because the contractor could not arrange adequate labour and materials in time. If extension of the completion period is granted for this delay, it will ordinarily be:

options.A: Granted without levy of liquidated damages, as the delay was unintentional
options.B: Granted with levy of liquidated damages for the period of delay attributable to the contractor
options.C: Refused in all cases, the contract being determined automatically
options.D: Granted together with payment of price variation at enhanced rates as compensation

e: Delay due solely to the contractor's failure to arrange labour and materials is attributable to him, so extension of time is ordinarily granted with levy of liquidated damages for that delay period under GCC.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where delay in completion is caused by the failure of the Railways to hand over the site or drawings in time, extension of time is granted without levy of liquidated damages.
2. Where delay is caused by the contractor's own default, extension of time is also granted without levy of liquidated damages as a matter of course.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: delay from Railways' failure to hand over site or drawings earns extension without liquidated damages; delay from contractor default does not get LD-free extension as a matter of course.

q: Where a works contract is determined on account of the contractor's default, the determination of the contract:

options.A: Wipes out all liabilities of the contractor which had accrued before the determination
options.B: Entitles the contractor to claim payment for work not yet executed by him
options.C: Does not release the contractor from the liabilities already accrued under the contract, including completion of the balance work at his risk and cost
options.D: Automatically cancels the bank guarantees furnished by the contractor

e: Determination for contractor default does not wipe out accrued liabilities; the contractor remains liable, including completion of balance work at his risk and cost, and guarantees are not automatically cancelled.

q: Under the arbitration clause of the General Conditions of Contract for Works, the arbitrator for deciding a dispute is appointed:

options.A: By the contractor from among his own representatives
options.B: By the Tender Committee which recommended the tender
options.C: By the civil court of the district in every case in the first instance
options.D: By the General Manager (or the competent appointing authority) from the panel of arbitrators maintained by the Railway administration

e: Under the GCC arbitration clause, the arbitrator is appointed by the General Manager or competent appointing authority from the panel of arbitrators maintained by the Railway administration.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A dispute relating to an 'excepted matter' under the General Conditions of Contract can be referred to arbitration like any other dispute.
2. For disputes other than excepted matters, the contractor invokes the arbitration clause by making a demand for arbitration in accordance with the contract conditions.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: excepted matters under GCC cannot be referred to arbitration, while other disputes are referred by the contractor making a demand for arbitration per the contract conditions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The materials which the Railways undertake to supply for a works contract are listed in a schedule forming part of the tender documents, together with the rates at which they will be charged to the contractor.
2. All materials other than those so listed are to be procured and brought to the site by the contractor at his own cost, as part of his contract obligation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: materials Railways undertake to supply are listed in a schedule in the tender documents with charge rates, and all other materials must be procured by the contractor at his own cost.

q: Departmental materials issued to a contractor for incorporation in a particular work are found to have been diverted by him to another work. The contractor is:

options.A: Entitled to use the materials on any work, as they become his property on issue
options.B: Required only to replace the materials at the end of the defect liability period
options.C: Liable to be charged for the materials at market rates of the other work
options.D: Accountable for the materials issued to him, and their value is recoverable from him in accordance with the contract conditions, the materials being meant only for the work for which they were issued

e: Departmental materials are issued only for the work for which they are given; the contractor is accountable for them and their value is recoverable per contract conditions if diverted to another work.

q: During the execution of a work, the contractor executes an additional item purely on a verbal request, without any written order of the Engineer for that item. As regards payment for that item, the contractor:

options.A: Becomes entitled to payment at his own rates as a matter of right
options.B: Cannot claim payment for it as a matter of right, extra items being payable when ordered in writing by the Engineer and settled in accordance with the contract
options.C: Must be paid at twice the schedule rate for the item
options.D: Can recover payment directly from the Tender Committee

e: Extra items are payable when ordered in writing by the Engineer and settled per the contract; an item done only on verbal request gives the contractor no right to payment at his own rates.

q: In a station building contract providing for ordinary flooring, the Engineer orders superior flooring to be laid in its place, in lieu of the flooring item originally provided. The superior flooring so executed is treated as:

options.A: A substituted item, its rate being settled in accordance with the provisions of the contract for substituted items
options.B: An altogether new work requiring a separate tender
options.C: A material modification of the sanctioned estimate in every case
options.D: Work done free of cost by the contractor

e: Superior flooring ordered in lieu of the flooring item originally provided is a substituted item, and its rate is settled under the GCC provisions for substituted items.

q: Entries made in the Site Order Book maintained at the site of a work represent:

options.A: The personal diary of the contractor's supervisor
options.B: The comparative statement of the tenders received for the work
options.C: The instructions of the Engineer or his representative to the contractor at the site, which the contractor is required to comply with and acknowledge
options.D: The record of hindrances encountered during the execution of the work

e: Entries in the Site Order Book are instructions of the Engineer or his representative to the contractor at site, which the contractor must comply with and acknowledge; hindrances go in the Hindrance Register.

q: Ordinary repairs and maintenance works chargeable to Revenue are sanctioned and executed:

options.A: Only after their individual inclusion in the Pink Book Works Programme as capital works
options.B: Against the funds allotted under the Capital grant for the year
options.C: Only with the sanction of the Railway Board in each individual case
options.D: By the competent executive authority against the revenue allotment for repairs and maintenance, and not through the capital Works Programme

e: Ordinary repairs and maintenance chargeable to Revenue are sanctioned and executed by the competent executive authority against the revenue allotment, not through the capital Pink Book Works Programme.

q: A small work of urgent repairs, within the monetary limit prescribed for minor works, is to be taken up against the lump-sum provision made for minor works. For its execution, it is necessary that:

options.A: The work is first individually listed in the Pink Book and sanctioned by the Railway Board
options.B: The work is sanctioned by the competent authority against that lump-sum provision, after its estimate is prepared and vetted as required
options.C: No estimate or sanction is needed for any minor work
options.D: A separate open tender is invited for the work in all cases

e: A minor work against lump-sum provision still needs its estimate prepared and vetted as required and sanction of the competent authority against that provision; it needs no individual Pink Book listing.

q: A bridge washout disrupts through traffic and restoration work is started at once on an urgency certificate, before a formal estimate is sanctioned. After the restoration, the expenditure so incurred is regularised by:

options.A: Treating the expenditure as a loss and writing it off without any sanction
options.B: Preparing the estimate for the work and obtaining the sanction of the competent authority for the expenditure, in accordance with the rules for urgent works
options.C: Recovering the expenditure from the contractor who executed the restoration
options.D: Charging the expenditure to the work of the following year without any report

e: Urgent restoration on an urgency certificate is regularised afterwards by preparing the estimate and obtaining sanction of the competent authority for the expenditure, per the rules for urgent works in the Engineering Code.

q: The correct sequence in the formation of the annual Works Programme of a Railway is:

options.A: Preliminary Works Programme submitted by the Zonal Railway, selection of works and issue of the Pink Book, and the Final Works Programme after the Demands for Grants are passed
options.B: Final Works Programme, Preliminary Works Programme, Pink Book
options.C: Pink Book, Final Works Programme, Preliminary Works Programme
options.D: Preliminary Works Programme, Final Works Programme, Pink Book

e: The sequence is: Preliminary Works Programme from the Zonal Railway, selection of works and issue of the Pink Book, then the Final Works Programme after the Demands for Grants are passed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Inclusion of a work in the List of Approved Works does not by itself dispense with the sanction of its detailed estimate by the competent authority before expenditure is incurred on it.
2. The List of Approved Works, forming Part II of the Pink Book, lists the works sanctioned by the Railway Board.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: inclusion in the List of Approved Works does not dispense with sanction of the detailed estimate; the List of Approved Works lists works sanctioned by the General Manager, not the Railway Board.

q: Licence fee and rent recovered by the Railways for the use of railway land given to outside parties for purposes connected with railway working, or on licence, are credited to:

options.A: Capital of the Railways
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Miscellaneous Deposits in the Public Account
options.D: The earnings (revenue receipts) of the Railways

e: Licence fee and rent for railway land given to outside parties for purposes connected with railway working or on licence are credited to earnings, that is revenue receipts of the Railways.

q: Before a private siding for a firm is constructed and opened for traffic:

options.A: No agreement of any kind is required with the firm
options.B: The firm is required only to give a verbal assurance to bear the charges
options.C: A formal siding agreement is executed between the Railways and the firm, under which the firm bears the cost of the siding and the charges payable for its maintenance and working
options.D: The siding is first opened and the agreement is executed after one year of working

e: Before a private siding is constructed and opened, a formal siding agreement is executed under which the firm bears the cost of the siding and charges for its maintenance and working by Railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In an EPC contract, the contractor prepares the detailed design of the project on the basis of the requirements and performance specifications given by the Railways.
2. In a traditional item-rate contract, the contractor executes the work in accordance with the designs and drawings furnished by the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: in an EPC contract the contractor designs on the basis of Railways' requirements and performance specifications, while in an item-rate contract he executes to designs furnished by Railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a DBFOT concession, the private partner designs, builds and finances the project at its own cost and risk.
2. In a DBFOT concession, the private partner operates the project during the concession period and transfers it to the authority at the end of that period.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: in DBFOT the private partner designs, builds and finances at its own cost and risk, operates during the concession period and transfers the project to the authority at its end.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A revised estimate is prepared when the cost of a sanctioned work is expected to exceed the sanctioned estimate materially.
2. A supplementary estimate is the estimate by which the original sanction for an altogether new work is obtained.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: a revised estimate is prepared when cost is expected to materially exceed the sanctioned estimate; a supplementary estimate covers additions to an existing work, not sanction for a new work.

q: The authority competent to sanction the estimate of a work is determined with reference to:

options.A: The amount of funds allotted for the work in the current year only
options.B: The total estimated cost of the work, in accordance with the Schedule of Powers
options.C: The value of the lowest tender received for the work
options.D: The amount of the contractor's first running bill

e: Competence to sanction an estimate is determined by the total estimated cost of the work under the Schedule of Powers, not by the current year's allotment, tender value or first bill amount.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. As a general rule, a work is not commenced before its detailed estimate has been sanctioned and funds have been allotted for it.
2. Works of restoration of through communication in an emergency may be commenced before the formal sanction of the estimate, the sanction being obtained subsequently.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: normally a work starts only after detailed estimate sanction and fund allotment, but restoration of through communication in an emergency may start before formal sanction, obtained subsequently.

q: Technical sanction to the detailed estimate of a work is accorded:

options.A: By the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer of the Railway
options.B: By the Tender Committee constituted for the work
options.C: By the Accounts Officer who will pass the bills of the work
options.D: By the competent engineering authority, after the detailed estimate has been prepared on the basis of detailed designs and drawings

e: Technical sanction is accorded by the competent engineering authority after the detailed estimate is prepared on detailed designs and drawings; it is not given by FA and CAO, Tender Committee or Accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Retention money is the amount withheld from the running bills of a contractor as a security for the due performance of the contract.
2. Retention money is the same as the earnest money refunded to the unsuccessful tenderers after the tender is decided.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: retention money is withheld from running bills as security for due performance; earnest money of unsuccessful tenderers is a separate tender-stage deposit refunded after decision.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On foreclosure (short-closure) of a contract, the balance work is completed at the risk and cost of the contractor.
2. On foreclosure of a contract, the contractor is paid for the work actually executed by him and for the materials taken over from him, as provided in the contract.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: on foreclosure the contractor is paid for work executed and materials taken over per the contract; balance work is not done at his risk and cost, that applying only to determination for default.

q: Where a small work is arranged on the basis of quotations, the quotations received are:

options.A: Accepted verbally without any record being kept
options.B: Tabulated in a comparative statement, and the work is awarded on a work order to the lowest reasonable quotation with the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: Referred to the Railway Board for acceptance in every case
options.D: Opened only after the work has been completed by the contractor

e: Quotations are tabulated in a comparative statement and the work is awarded on a work order to the lowest reasonable quotation with sanction of the competent authority; verbal, unrecorded acceptance is not allowed.

q: The Hindrance Register maintained for a works contract is required to be signed, in token of the hindrances recorded in it, by:

options.A: The Accounts Officer passing the bills of the work
options.B: The members of the Tender Committee
options.C: The contractor alone, in his own office
options.D: The representative of the Engineer and the representative of the contractor at the site

e: The Hindrance Register must be signed by the representative of the Engineer and the representative of the contractor at site, in token of the hindrances recorded for the contract.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An excess of the final cost of a work over its sanctioned estimate is regularised at the work level through the completion report or a revised estimate, with the sanction of the competent authority.
2. An excess of expenditure over the grant voted by Parliament is a matter at the grant level, which is brought before Parliament for regularisation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: excess of final cost over a sanctioned estimate is regularised at work level through completion report or revised estimate, while excess over the grant voted by Parliament is regularised at grant level before Parliament.

q: In a public-private partnership concession for a railway project, the concession period granted to the private partner ordinarily covers:

options.A: The construction period together with the period of operation of the facility by the partner, at the end of which the facility is transferred to the authority
options.B: Only the period required for the construction of the project
options.C: Only the defect liability period of the works executed
options.D: The period up to the issue of the Letter of Acceptance to the partner

e: In a PPP concession the concession period covers construction plus operation of the facility by the partner, at the end of which the facility is transferred to the authority.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The owner of a private siding pays licence fee for the railway land occupied by the siding, where railway land is used for it.
2. The owner of a private siding bears the maintenance charges of the portion of the siding which is maintained by the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the private siding owner pays licence fee for railway land occupied and bears maintenance charges for the portion of the siding maintained by Railways, per the siding agreement.

q: Before a deposit work is taken up for execution on behalf of an outside body, the estimate prepared for the work is:

options.A: Never shown to the body on whose behalf the work is to be executed
options.B: Sanctioned only after the work has been completed and its cost ascertained
options.C: Adjusted against the earnings of the Railways in the first instance
options.D: Communicated to the body concerned for its acceptance, and the work is taken up after the estimated amount, including departmental charges, is deposited by it

e: For a deposit work the estimate is communicated to the outside body for acceptance, and work is taken up only after the estimated amount including departmental charges is deposited by it.

q: 'Abstract cost data', used in connection with the preparation of estimates of works, refers to:

options.A: The rates quoted by contractors in tenders for similar works in the past
options.B: Data compiled from the actual cost of similar works already executed, analysed per unit of measurement, which is used for framing abstract estimates of similar proposed works
options.C: The schedule of rates of the Railway for items of work
options.D: The data of departmental charges leviable on works executed for outside bodies

e: Abstract cost data are compiled from actual cost of similar works already executed, analysed per unit of measurement, and are used for framing abstract estimates of similar proposed works.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An abstract estimate of a proposed building work can be framed with the help of abstract cost data of similar buildings already executed.
2. Abstract cost data are kept useful by revising them from time to time to reflect changes in the cost of materials and labour.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: abstract estimates can be framed from abstract cost data of similar executed buildings, and the data are kept useful by periodic revision for changes in material and labour costs.

q: A sanction accorded to the estimate of a work is not acted upon, and the work is not commenced within the period for which the sanction remains current. The correct position is that:

options.A: The sanction continues indefinitely and the work may be commenced at any time thereafter
options.B: The work may be commenced and the sanction treated as automatically renewed
options.C: The sanction lapses on the expiry of its currency, and the work can be commenced only after the sanction is revalidated or a fresh sanction is obtained
options.D: The sanction is deemed to have been converted into a sanction for the following year

e: Sanction has a limited currency; if the work is not commenced within it, the sanction lapses and the work can start only after revalidation or fresh sanction.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A lapsed sanction to a work can be revalidated by the original sanctioning authority even where the cost of the work, as now estimated, exceeds the powers of that authority.
2. Where the cost on revalidation exceeds the powers of the original sanctioning authority, the sanction of the authority competent for that total cost is required.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: if cost on revalidation exceeds the powers of the original sanctioning authority, sanction of the authority competent for that total cost is required for revalidation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The lapse of the annual allotment of funds at the close of a financial year does not, by itself, cancel the sanction accorded to the estimate of a work which is in progress.
2. Expenditure on such a work in the following year requires a fresh allotment of funds for that year, the sanction alone not being sufficient.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: lapse of annual fund allotment at year end does not cancel the estimate sanction of a work in progress, but next year's expenditure needs a fresh allotment; sanction alone is not enough.

q: 'Check measurement' of work done by a contractor, as distinct from the original measurement recorded in the Measurement Book, is:

options.A: The measurement of the work recorded by the contractor himself
options.B: The measurement recorded for the purpose of preparing the abstract estimate of the work
options.C: A second measurement of the same work carried out for the purpose of the contractor's final bill only
options.D: An independent verification, by a superior or authorised official, of the measurements already recorded, carried out before payment to guard against error or over-measurement

e: Check measurement is independent verification by a superior or authorised official of measurements already recorded, done before payment to guard against error or over-measurement.

q: The measurements of a costly item of work recorded by a junior engineer are got check-measured by a senior official before the running bill is passed. The main object of this check measurement is to:

options.A: Enable the contractor to claim a higher rate for the item
options.B: Verify independently that the quantities recorded are correct, so that payment is not made for work not actually executed
options.C: Reduce the quantities recorded in every case by a fixed percentage
options.D: Substitute the senior official's measurements for the tendered quantities in the agreement

e: Check measurement of a costly item independently verifies that recorded quantities are correct, so payment is not made for work not actually executed; it does not change rates or tendered quantities.

q: An audit objection raised on the accounts of a work points out an overpayment made to a contractor. The objection is finally settled when:

options.A: The executive merely records that the objection has been noted for future guidance
options.B: The amount is charged to another work of the division
options.C: The contractor agrees to execute additional work free of cost at some future date
options.D: The overpayment is recovered from the contractor or otherwise regularised with the sanction of the competent authority, and Audit is satisfied accordingly

e: An audit objection for overpayment is settled only when the overpayment is recovered from the contractor or otherwise regularised with competent sanction and Audit is satisfied; mere noting is not settlement.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Statutory audit conducts periodical inspections of divisional and executive offices, in which works transactions are also examined, and communicates its findings through inspection reports.
2. A para of an audit inspection report relating to a work can be treated as closed by the executive on its own, without sending a reply to Audit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: statutory audit inspects offices and communicates findings through inspection reports; a para cannot be closed by the executive on its own without sending a reply to Audit.

q: In the course of a tender for a major work, circumstances come to notice which prima facie suggest malpractice by tenderers. The proper course is that:

options.A: The matter may be brought to the notice of the Vigilance organisation for investigation, while the decision on the tender itself rests with the competent authority on the merits of the case
options.B: The tender must be awarded at once to the lowest tenderer, vigilance action being irrelevant to tenders
options.C: All the tenderers must be debarred permanently without any enquiry
options.D: The Vigilance organisation itself accepts the tender in place of the Tender Committee

e: Suspected malpractice in a tender is brought to the Vigilance organisation for investigation, while the tender decision itself rests with the competent authority on merits; Vigilance does not accept tenders.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is used primarily for the procurement of goods and of common services through an online marketplace.
2. IREPS is the Railways' own e-procurement system through which works tenders and stores tenders of the Railways are invited and processed online.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: GeM is the online marketplace mainly for goods and common services, while IREPS is Railways' own e-procurement system for works and stores tenders.

q: A work is deliberately divided into a number of small parcels, each kept within the financial powers of a lower authority, although the work could conveniently be executed as a whole. This course is objectionable because it amounts to:

options.A: A material modification of the sanctioned estimate
options.B: A variation within the meaning of the General Conditions of Contract
options.C: Foreclosure of the larger work
options.D: Splitting of the work to evade the sanction of the higher authority and the tender procedure applicable to the work as a whole

e: Dividing one work into small parcels within a lower authority's powers, though it could be executed as a whole, is splitting to evade higher sanction and the applicable tender procedure, and is prohibited.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where a contract is closed on the ground that the work is no longer required by the Railways, and not on account of any default of the contractor, the contractor is paid for the work actually executed by him as provided in the contract, and the balance work is not got done at his risk and cost.
2. In such a closure for the Railways' own reasons, the extra cost of completing the balance work through another agency is recoverable from the contractor.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: on closure because Railways no longer need the work, the contractor is paid for work actually executed per contract and balance work is not at his risk and cost; statement 2 is therefore false.

q: Under the price variation clause of a works contract, the 'base' indices with which the indices for the period of execution are compared are:

options.A: The indices prevailing on the date of the final bill of the work
options.B: The indices prevailing on the date of completion of the work
options.C: The indices for the base period specified in the contract, ordinarily referable to the period around the submission of the tender
options.D: The indices of the year in which the estimate of the work was sanctioned

e: Under the price variation clause, indices for the execution period are compared with base indices for the base period specified in the contract, ordinarily around the time of tender submission.

q: A works contract contains a price variation clause. During execution, the relevant price indices fall appreciably below the base indices. The consequence under the clause is that:

options.A: No adjustment is made, price variation operating only when indices rise
options.B: The contractor is paid the same amount as would have been payable at the base indices
options.C: The contract is determined and re-tendered at lower rates
options.D: The price variation works out as a negative amount, and the sum payable to the contractor is reduced, or the amount recovered from his bills, accordingly

e: Price variation works both ways: if indices fall below base indices, variation is negative and the amount payable to the contractor is reduced or recovered from his bills accordingly.

q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised type of advance payable to a works contractor under the General Conditions of Contract?

options.A: Advance against the wages which will become payable to the contractor's labour in the following month
options.B: Secured advance against materials brought to the site for incorporation in the work
options.C: Mobilisation advance payable at the commencement of the work
options.D: Advance against new plant and machinery brought to the site for use on the work

e: Advance against next month's labour wages is not a recognised GCC advance; recognised advances are secured advance on materials, mobilisation advance and advance against new plant and machinery brought to site.

q: Payment made to a contractor on a running (on-account) bill does not, by itself, amount to:

options.A: An interim payment adjustable at the final settlement of the contract
options.B: A final and conclusive acceptance that the work paid for fully conforms to the contract in every respect, barring all later recovery
options.C: A payment based on the measurements recorded for the work done up to that stage
options.D: A payment from which the recoveries due to the Railways can be effected

e: Payment on a running bill is only an interim payment based on measurements and subject to recoveries; it does not amount to final and conclusive acceptance barring all later recovery.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. During the defect liability period of a completed work, defects which appear and are pointed out to the contractor are to be rectified by him at his own cost.
2. The ordinary day-to-day maintenance of an asset after it has been taken over is the responsibility of the department maintaining it, and is distinct from the rectification of defects by the contractor during the defect liability period.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: during the defect liability period the contractor rectifies defects pointed out at his own cost, while ordinary day-to-day maintenance after taking over is the maintaining department's responsibility.

q: During the execution of a station building work, several changes from the original drawings are ordered and carried out. On completion of the work, the drawings of the work must be:

options.A: Destroyed, the original tender drawings alone being retained on record
options.B: Corrected and completed to show the work exactly as actually executed, such corrected drawings being preserved as the record drawings of the asset
options.C: Corrected only if Audit raises an objection on the work
options.D: Left uncorrected, the changes being recorded only in the contractor's final bill

e: On completion, drawings must be corrected to show the work exactly as executed and preserved as record drawings of the asset; changes cannot remain recorded only in the final bill.

q: Before the Notice Inviting Tender for a work is issued, the tender documents are ordinarily got vetted by the Finance/Accounts branch primarily in order to ensure that:

options.A: The lowest rate to be accepted for the work is fixed in advance
options.B: The names of the firms to whom the work may be given are decided
options.C: The contractor who will execute the work is selected beforehand
options.D: The eligibility conditions, security requirements, price variation and other financial conditions proposed to be included are in order and in accordance with the rules

e: Finance vetting of tender documents before NIT ensures eligibility conditions, security requirements, price variation and other financial conditions are in order and in accordance with the rules.

q: The cost of a sanctioned work rises during execution only on account of increases in the prices of materials and labour, there being no change in its scope or design. The excess over the sanctioned estimate is regularised by:

options.A: Treating the work as a new work and inviting fresh tenders for it
options.B: Recovering the excess from the contractor executing the work
options.C: Getting a revised estimate, or the completion report, sanctioned by the authority competent to sanction the total cost of the work, explaining the reasons for the excess
options.D: Booking the excess to a suspense head permanently

e: Excess due only to price rises, with no scope or design change, is regularised by a revised estimate or completion report sanctioned by the authority competent for the total cost, explaining the reasons.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The provision for contingencies in a sanctioned estimate can be used to add an altogether new facility which was not contemplated in the sanctioned scope of the work.
2. Petty and unforeseen items arising in the course of execution, which are within the sanctioned scope and do not take the total cost beyond the sanctioned estimate, can be met from the provision for contingencies.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: contingencies cover petty unforeseen items within the sanctioned scope that do not breach the sanctioned total; they cannot fund an altogether new facility outside the scope.

q: The Departmental and General (D&G) charges provided in connection with a work broadly comprise:

options.A: The profit of the contractor and his overhead charges
options.B: The cost of materials and labour required for the work
options.C: The earnest money and security deposit of the contractor
options.D: Establishment (supervision) charges and tools and plant charges

e: Departmental and General (D and G) charges in an estimate broadly comprise establishment or supervision charges and tools and plant charges, not contractor profit, material cost or deposits.

q: A work is completed and its completion report is under preparation, but the work-charged establishment sanctioned for the work continues to be employed and its cost continues to be booked to the work. This is irregular because:

options.A: Work-charged establishment is sanctioned for the specific work and must be wound up, or transferred with proper sanction, on completion of the work; its cost cannot continue to be charged to a completed work
options.B: Work-charged establishment should always be converted into permanent establishment on completion of a work
options.C: The cost of work-charged establishment is never chargeable to a work
options.D: The establishment should have been provided by the contractor executing the work

e: Work-charged establishment is sanctioned for the specific work and must be wound up or transferred with proper sanction on completion; charging its cost to a completed work is irregular.

q: Departmental tools and plant are issued to a contractor for use on a work on hire under the agreement. During the work, a machine is damaged through the contractor's negligence. In such a case:

options.A: The loss falls on the Railways, the tools and plant being departmental property
options.B: Hire charges for the period of use are recoverable from the contractor, and the cost of making good the damage caused by his negligence is also recoverable from him under the agreement
options.C: The contractor may retain the damaged machine in lieu of his security deposit
options.D: The damage is adjusted against the departmental charges of the work

e: For departmental tools and plant hired to the contractor, hire charges for the period of use and the cost of making good damage caused by his negligence are both recoverable from him under the agreement.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A suspense head must not be used merely to park expenditure on a work so as to avoid showing an excess over the sanctioned estimate or over the allotment.
2. Expenditure which is genuinely recoverable from another party, or which is awaiting final adjustment, is initially booked under the appropriate suspense head pending its clearance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a suspense head must not be used to park expenditure to hide excess over estimate or allotment, but genuinely recoverable or awaiting-adjustment expenditure is initially booked there pending clearance.

q: The Final Location Survey of a proposed new railway line, as compared with the earlier surveys, is the stage at which:

options.A: The alignment of the line is finally fixed and marked on the ground, and detailed data and drawings are obtained on which the detailed estimate of the line is based
options.B: Only a rough cost of the line is worked out from cost data of other lines
options.C: The proposal is examined only to decide whether it is prima facie worth taking up
options.D: Only the traffic prospects of the line are assessed in general terms

e: At Final Location Survey the alignment is finally fixed and marked on the ground and detailed data and drawings are obtained on which the detailed estimate of the line is based.

q: Under a 'non-comprehensive' Annual Maintenance Contract for equipment such as lifts or air-conditioning plants, as distinguished from a comprehensive contract:

options.A: The contracting agency provides the maintenance service, while the spare parts replaced during maintenance are supplied, or paid for, by the Railways
options.B: The contracting agency bears the cost of all spare parts replaced during maintenance
options.C: The Railways provide the labour and the agency only supplies spare parts
options.D: No payment is made to the agency until the equipment is replaced as a whole

e: Under a non-comprehensive AMC the agency provides only the maintenance service, while spare parts replaced are supplied or paid for by Railways; in a comprehensive contract the agency bears spares cost too.

q: On the completion of a work charged to Capital, the cost of the asset created is capitalised, which means that:

options.A: The cost is written off to Revenue in the year of completion
options.B: The cost continues to be shown indefinitely as expenditure on a work in progress
options.C: The amount is recovered from the department which will use the asset
options.D: The completed cost is brought into the capital-at-charge of the Railways and recorded asset-wise in the Block Account/asset records, the work-in-progress position being cleared

e: On completion of a capital work its cost is capitalised: it is brought into capital-at-charge and recorded asset-wise in the Block Account and asset records, clearing the work-in-progress position.

q: A works contract can be treated as finally closed when:

options.A: The first running bill of the contractor has been paid
options.B: The Letter of Acceptance issued for the work has expired
options.C: The final bill has been settled, the completion certificate issued, the defect liability period has run its course and the security deposit/performance guarantee has been released after adjustment of all dues
options.D: The contractor has submitted his tender for the next work of the division

e: A contract is finally closed only when the final bill is settled, completion certificate issued, defect liability period has run its course and security deposit or performance guarantee is released after adjusting all dues.

q: During a periodical verification of railway land plans and boundaries, an unauthorised occupation of railway land is detected. The action to be taken is that:

options.A: The occupation is regularised automatically on payment of the current year's licence fee
options.B: The land is treated as surrendered to the occupant if the occupation is old
options.C: The engineering staff demolish the structure on their own without any proceedings
options.D: The matter is reported and proceedings for eviction of the unauthorised occupant are initiated before the Estate Officer under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act

e: Unauthorised occupation of railway land is reported and eviction proceedings are initiated before the Estate Officer under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act; it is not regularised automatically.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A way-leave permission over railway land creates a transferable interest in the land in favour of the person to whom it is granted.
2. A way-leave is only a permission to cross or use railway land for a specified purpose, such as laying a pipeline or a road, on payment of the prescribed charges, and creates no interest in the land.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: way-leave is only permission to cross or use railway land for a specified purpose on prescribed charges and creates no interest in the land, so it is not a transferable interest.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A detailed estimate of a work is accompanied by a report explaining the proposal, its necessity and how its cost has been arrived at.
2. The specifications forming part of a detailed estimate/contract define the quality of materials, the workmanship and the manner in which the work is to be executed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a detailed estimate carries a report explaining the proposal, necessity and cost build-up, and its specifications define quality of materials, workmanship and manner of execution.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure which merely restores an existing asset to its original standard, without enhancing its capacity, is in the nature of a renewal or repair of that asset.
2. Expenditure which improves an asset to a higher standard or enhances its capacity is also treated as ordinary repair in every case, the element of improvement being ignored.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: expenditure merely restoring an asset to its original standard is renewal or repair; improvement to a higher standard or capacity cannot be treated as ordinary repair ignoring the improvement element.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The estimate of a work is framed at the rates given in the schedule of rates.
2. Payment to the contractor for the work is made at the rates agreed in the contract, which may be above or below the schedule rates on which the estimate was framed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: estimates are framed at schedule of rates, while contractor payment is at agreed contract rates, which may be above or below schedule rates.

q: Individual work orders under a zonal contract for petty works and repairs can be issued only:

options.A: For works of any value, the zonal contract having no ceiling
options.B: After inviting fresh open tenders for each petty work
options.C: With the prior sanction of the Railway Board in each case
options.D: Up to the value limit prescribed for work orders in that contract; a work beyond that limit has to be arranged through the procedure applicable to works of that value

e: Work orders under a zonal contract can be issued only up to the prescribed value limit for work orders in that contract; a work beyond it must follow the procedure for works of that value.

q: In e-tendering through IREPS, the bids submitted by tenderers for a work remain protected before the due date and time of opening in that:

options.A: They can be opened and read by the tender-opening officials at any time after submission
options.B: They are visible to all other tenderers as soon as they are submitted
options.C: They can be modified by the executive office after submission
options.D: They are held in sealed/encrypted form and can be opened only on or after the due date and time by the authorised officials

e: In IREPS e-tendering, bids are held in sealed and encrypted form and can be opened only on or after the due date and time by authorised officials; they are not visible or alterable earlier.

q: Expenditure on a work is found, on internal check, to have been booked under a wrong allocation head. The error is set right by:

options.A: A book (transfer) adjustment correcting the allocation to the proper head, carried out with the approval required for such corrections
options.B: Altering the sanctioned estimate of the work to match the head actually debited
options.C: Recovering the amount of the work from the contractor
options.D: Letting the error stand, as the total expenditure of the Railway is unaffected

e: Wrong allocation is set right by a book or transfer adjustment to the proper head with the approval required for such corrections; the estimate, contractor or total expenditure is not altered for it.

q: A work has been completed, its completion report has been sanctioned and its final accounts have been settled. Thereafter:

options.A: Further expenditure can continue to be booked to the work as long as its estimate is on record
options.B: The balance of the work can be transferred to the contractor's ledger permanently
options.C: The work is closed in the Works Register, and no further expenditure is booked to that work
options.D: The work is reopened automatically in the following financial year

e: Once the completion report is sanctioned and final accounts settled, the work is closed in the Works Register and no further expenditure can be booked to that work.

q: In respect of the labour engaged by him on a railway work, a contractor is prohibited from:

options.A: Paying wages through a bank account of the workmen
options.B: Engaging labour residing outside the district in which the work is situated
options.C: Maintaining muster rolls of the labour engaged by him
options.D: Employing child labour on the work, in contravention of the law prohibiting such employment

e: A contractor is prohibited from employing child labour on a railway work in contravention of the law; bank payment of wages and maintaining muster rolls are lawful requirements, not prohibitions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The routine upkeep of equipment, arranged through an Annual Maintenance Contract, is in the nature of a works contract for the renewal of that equipment.
2. Renewal or replacement of an asset is executed as a work, whereas the routine maintenance of equipment under an Annual Maintenance Contract is arranged as a services contract.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: renewal or replacement of an asset is executed as a work, while routine upkeep under an Annual Maintenance Contract is a services contract, not a works contract for renewal.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Preventive vigilance in tendering lays emphasis on transparency of procedure and on system improvements which reduce the scope for corruption, and not merely on action after an irregularity has occurred.
2. Vigilance in connection with tenders is concerned only with the punishment of officers after a tender has been awarded.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: preventive vigilance stresses transparency and system improvements that reduce scope for corruption, not merely punishment after an irregularity.

q: Where a works tender is submitted by a joint venture, the member designated as the lead member of the joint venture is the member who:

options.A: Is exempt from all liability for the execution of the work
options.B: Is authorised under the joint venture agreement to act, correspond and receive instructions on behalf of the joint venture in dealings with the Railways
options.C: Alone furnishes the earnest money and is solely liable for the whole work
options.D: Decides the rates to be quoted by the other members for their portions

e: The lead member of a joint venture is authorised under the JV agreement to act, correspond and receive instructions on behalf of the venture in dealings with Railways.

q: In the analysis of rates for an item of work whose rate is not available in the schedule of rates, provision is made, in addition to the cost of materials, labour and tools and plant for the item, for:

options.A: The earnest money deposited by the contractor for the work
options.B: The departmental charges of the Railways on the work
options.C: The liquidated damages leviable under the contract
options.D: The contractor's overheads and profit on the item

e: Rate analysis for a non-schedule item provides, besides materials, labour and tools and plant, for the contractor's overheads and profit on the item.

q: The abstract of estimated cost given at the end of a detailed estimate of a work serves to:

options.A: Summarise the cost of the work sub-head-wise and, after adding the provisions such as contingencies and Departmental and General charges, arrive at the total estimated cost of the work for sanction
options.B: Record the rates finally quoted by the tenderers for the work
options.C: Compare the cost of the work with the earnings expected from it in the first year
options.D: List the works included in the Works Programme for the year

e: The abstract of estimated cost summarises the work sub-head-wise and, after adding contingencies and Departmental and General charges, arrives at the total estimated cost for sanction.

q: An approximate estimate of a proposed building is prepared by the cubical content method. Under this method, the rough cost of the building is arrived at by:

options.A: Multiplying the plinth area of the building by the rate per unit of plinth area
options.B: Taking a fixed amount for each person who will occupy the building
options.C: Adding up the detailed quantities of each item of work at schedule rates
options.D: Multiplying the total cubic content (volume) of the building by the rate per unit volume derived from similar buildings

e: Under the cubical content method, rough cost equals total cubic content or volume of the building multiplied by the rate per unit volume derived from similar buildings.

q: The service unit method of preparing an approximate estimate is commonly adopted for buildings such as hospitals, hostels and schools because, under this method:

options.A: The cost is worked out item-wise from the drawings of the building
options.B: The cost is taken as a percentage of the cost of the land
options.C: The cost is estimated per unit of service, such as per bed in a hospital or per student in a hostel, on the basis of the cost of similar buildings already executed
options.D: No estimate is required for such buildings at all

e: Under the service unit method, cost is estimated per unit of service, such as per bed in a hospital or per student in a hostel, from cost of similar buildings already executed.

q: 'Prime cost' items provided in a detailed estimate are items in respect of which:

options.A: The work is to be executed departmentally without any contractor
options.B: A lump provision is made in the estimate for articles or fittings whose exact pattern and price are not finally settled at the estimate stage, the actual cost being adjusted at the time of execution
options.C: The contractor is paid in advance before the work starts
options.D: The rates are fixed personally by the sanctioning authority

e: Prime cost items carry a lump provision for articles or fittings whose exact pattern and price are not settled at estimate stage, the actual cost being adjusted during execution.

q: The 'details of measurements' which accompany a detailed estimate show:

options.A: The measurements of work actually executed by the contractor at site
options.B: The comparative statement of the tenders received for the work
options.C: The item-wise working of the quantities provided in the estimate, as calculated from the drawings and designs of the proposed work
options.D: The measurements recorded in the Measurement Book of an earlier work

e: Details of measurements accompanying a detailed estimate show the item-wise working of quantities provided in the estimate, calculated from drawings and designs of the proposed work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A reconnaissance survey of a proposed railway line is a rapid preliminary examination, made with the help of available maps and field inspection, to select the broad corridor or corridors worthy of detailed survey.
2. A reconnaissance survey by itself furnishes the detailed data on which the detailed estimate of the line is framed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: reconnaissance is a rapid preliminary examination using maps and field inspection to select broad corridors for detailed survey; it does not furnish data for the detailed estimate.

q: The expenditure incurred during the construction period of a major project, including the interest payable on the capital borrowed for the project during that period, is treated as:

options.A: Revenue expenditure of the years in which it is incurred
options.B: A loss to be written off when the project is opened
options.C: Part of the capital cost of the project, being capitalised along with the cost of the assets created
options.D: An advance recoverable from the contractor executing the project

e: Construction-period expenditure including interest on capital borrowed during construction is part of the capital cost of the project and is capitalised with the cost of assets created.

q: Initial spares, special tools and accessories which are supplied along with, and as part of, a newly procured machine or asset are treated in accounts as:

options.A: Revenue stores consumed in the year of purchase
options.B: An item of the Material-at-Site account of an unrelated work
options.C: A deposit to be kept with the supplier
options.D: Part of the capital cost of the asset itself

e: Initial spares, special tools and accessories supplied along with and as part of a new machine are part of the capital cost of the asset itself, not revenue stores.

q: The Fixed Asset Register maintained by a Railway is periodically reconciled with the Block Account and the capital-at-charge figures in the Finance Accounts primarily in order to ensure that:

options.A: The assets recorded asset-wise agree with the capital cost booked in the accounts, and differences are located and set right
options.B: The contractors' ledgers agree with the Works Register
options.C: The earnings of the Railway agree with the Traffic Book
options.D: The stores balances agree with the price ledgers

e: Reconciliation of the Fixed Asset Register with the Block Account and capital-at-charge in Finance Accounts ensures asset-wise records agree with capital cost booked, and differences are located and set right.

q: The licence fee charged for railway land licensed to an outside party is assessed primarily with reference to:

options.A: The profit earned by the licensee from the land
options.B: A uniform flat amount for all categories of land all over the Railways
options.C: The licence fees charged by the neighbouring municipal body for its own lands in all cases
options.D: The value of the land licensed and the purpose for which it is used, in accordance with the policy in force

e: Licence fee for railway land is assessed with reference to the value of the land licensed and the purpose of use, per the policy in force, not the licensee's profit or a uniform flat amount.

q: A party holding a way-leave permission has laid a pipeline across railway land. The Railways later require that portion of land for their own work. In such a case, as per the usual conditions of the permission:

options.A: The Railways must purchase the land from the party before using it
options.B: The party acquires a permanent right and cannot be asked to shift the pipeline
options.C: The party is required to shift or remove the pipeline at its own cost when so required by the Railways, the permission creating no interest in the land
options.D: The cost of shifting is borne by the Railways in all cases

e: Under way-leave conditions the party must shift or remove its pipeline at its own cost when Railways require the land, the permission creating no interest in the land.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where a discrepancy is found in a tender between the rate quoted by the tenderer in words and the rate quoted in figures, the rate in words is ordinarily taken as the correct rate.
2. Where the amount worked out for an item differs from the product of its quantity and unit rate, the unit rate quoted is ordinarily taken as governing.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct tender evaluation rules: where words and figures differ, the rate in words ordinarily governs, and where the item amount differs from quantity x rate, the unit rate quoted ordinarily governs.

q: Where a tender for a work is submitted by a joint venture, the technical credentials and financial capacity relied upon for deciding the eligibility of the joint venture are assessed:

options.A: Only on the basis of the credentials of the lead member, the other members being ignored
options.B: By pooling the relevant credentials and capacities of the members of the joint venture, as permitted by the tender conditions
options.C: Only on the basis of the member holding the smallest share in the venture
options.D: Without reference to any member's past experience, the venture being a new entity

e: Eligibility of a joint venture is assessed by pooling the relevant technical credentials and financial capacities of its members as permitted by the tender conditions, not on the lead member alone.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before tenders are invited for a work, the tenderers must be allowed adequate time, having regard to the nature and scope of the work, for inspecting the site and preparing and submitting their offers.
2. The time allowed for submission of tenders may be curtailed to any extent at the discretion of the executive, without recording any reasons.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: tenderers must get adequate time, considering nature and scope, to inspect the site and submit offers; time cannot be curtailed arbitrarily without recording reasons.

q: Clarifications issued to tenderers after a pre-bid conference for a major work take effect by being:

options.A: Communicated orally to the tenderers who attended the conference only
options.B: Issued in writing to all the tenderers as a corrigendum/addendum, which then forms part of the tender documents
options.C: Recorded only in the personal diary of the convening officer
options.D: Incorporated in the agreement after the work is awarded, without informing the tenderers

e: Pre-bid clarifications take effect only when issued in writing to all tenderers as a corrigendum or addendum forming part of the tender documents, not by oral communication to attendees only.

q: In evaluating the financial bids of technically qualified tenderers for a works tender, the Tender Committee ordinarily compares the tenderers on the basis of:

options.A: The lowest rate quoted by each tenderer for any single item of the work
options.B: The rates quoted in the tenderers' earlier contracts with other Railways
options.C: The earnest money furnished by each tenderer
options.D: The total evaluated cost of the work as a whole on the rates quoted by each tenderer

e: The Tender Committee compares technically qualified tenderers on the total evaluated cost of the work as a whole on rates quoted by each, not on any single item rate, earlier contracts or earnest money.
